read.thesis: Q4 acute same-facility EBITDA margin rose 50bp to 14.8% on labor and supply control, but 2026 guidance embeds a ~$75m exchange headwind and ~$35m California staffing cost; volumes flat in Q4.

capex.quote: We expect capital expenditures in 2026 to range between $950 million and $1.1 billion, reflecting the culmination of spending for several large inpatient projects that will come online during the first half of 2026.

triggers.label: Acute pricing guided 3%-4% for 2026
triggers.quote: our guidance implies a 3% to 4% pricing increase. That's in line.

triggers.label: Operating cash flow fell to $1.9B from $2.1B
triggers.quote: Cash generated from operating activities was $1.9 billion for the 12 months ended December 31, 2025, as compared to $2.1 billion during 2024.

triggers.label: Exchange volumes to fall 25%-30%
triggers.quote: we assume that exchange volumes will decline by 25% to 30%

triggers.label: Behavioral volume growth 1.5% in Q4
triggers.quote: a 1.5% increase in same-facility adjusted patient days

guidance.quote: We expect revenue to range between $18.4 billion and $18.8 billion, representing growth of 6% to 8%.
We expect adjusted EBITDA net of NCI to range between $2.64 billion and $2.79 billion, representing growth of 2% to 8%.
We expect adjusted net income attributable to UHS per diluted share to range between $22.64 and $24.52
Our guidance assumes same-facility volume growth to be in a range of 2% to 3% for both segments for the full year 2026
We expect capital expenditures in 2026 to range between $950 million and $1.1 billion

red_flags.label: Exchange premium non-payment bad debt risk
red_flags.quote: they don't pay -- they won't reimburse the charges at that point.

red_flags.label: Operating cash flow down on receivables and Medicaid timing
red_flags.quote: $145 million related to the timing of payments for certain Medicaid supplemental programs.

evasions.quote: it's impossible to precisely quantify -- even precisely quantify what we've been able to achieve
it's not an accident that none of the hospital companies have really attempted to quantify
